claims: Most title plans show the general position rather than the exact legal line of a boundary.
There is no standard tolerance, measurement or ratio linking the general boundary line on a title plan to the legal boundary.
Survey accuracy and physical features may inform interpretation but cannot promote an index polygon to an exact legal boundary.
A determined boundary is recorded with points or plan detail showing the extent whose exact line has been determined.
Boundary agreements and determined-boundary applications have separate evidential and plan requirements.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are updated monthly.
Each polygon has a Land Registry-INSPIRE ID related to a registered title.

official_sources.authority: HM Land Registry Use land and property data
claims: An index polygon may be the same size, larger or smaller than the extent shown on the title plan.
INSPIRE Index Polygons are a subset of the National Polygon Dataset and remain an index representation rather than proof of the exact legal boundary.

quality_guards: Do not claim centimetre-level or map-scale legal-boundary accuracy from a general title plan.
Do not equate a unique INSPIRE ID with exact candidate identity unless the current polygon and title linkage bytes are captured.
Preserve monthly release and local-authority duplicate semantics when reconciling polygons.
Fail closed until current Barnet/Enfield polygon bytes, title linkage and candidate-specific INSPIRE IDs are read back.
evidence_digest_policy: GitHub remote blob SHA readback after publish
